12.1e — Grid/Symmetry Jam: Showcase

The third arcade row of the year, and the last one with new games for a while. Grid games are the most SPECTATOR-friendly genre: passersby understand them in one glance, which makes today's showcase the most watchable yet. Star votes, retro, and then the road ahead.

Showcase ~30 min

Arcade row (10.1f contract): host and player in equal measure, pitch sticky by every keyboard. Star categories, grid edition:

  • BEST BOARD: which game was understandable in one glance — the purest grid virtue
  • BEST SYMMETRY: where did the mirroring create fairness, difficulty, or beauty instead of just... mirroring
  • BEST RULE: which single rule did the most work per line of code

Count the grid-game-only data: which game had the most passersby STOP (the one-glance test, live)?

Retro ~15 min

The four quadrants (10.1f format), plus the grid-jam question:

  1. Went well / went wrong — one process fact each, with evidence
  2. The grid discovery: what did the GRID give you that free movement would not have? (Every constraint jam had one — this is the constraint's receipt.)
  3. The year-in-games question: compare your three jams (2-button, cards, grid). Which jam's CONSTRAINT taught you the most — and why does the answer usually rhyme with "the one that made me finish" (9.3 tradeoffs, artistic edition)?

Tinker: Archive + look ahead

  1. git tag jam-grid && git push --tags; RETRO.md update with star counts and the grid-discovery sentence.
  2. Read the room's next dates on the dashboard: two placeholder flex days (12.2a, 12.2b) close the year — topic TBA until then. Bring your grid jam's best idea; the placeholder jam may want it.

Reflect: three constraints, one lesson

Of the three jams you shipped this year, which constraint taught you the most about finishing — and what would you tell a team choosing their own constraint for a fourth jam?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Host + play with star votes and stopper-counts
  • Name your grid discovery in one sentence
  • Rank your three jams by what their constraints taught
  • Leave a tagged repo and an honest RETRO.md
